title: Graph overlays on an iris UMAP
text: four numeric columns iris go UMAP. two extras worth keeping ranked neighbors (ret_nn = TRUE) fitted fuzzy graph (ret_extra = "fgraph"). plots use one saved run code.
code: X <- as.matrix(iris[, 1:4]) set.seed(65) fit <- uwot::umap(   X,   n_neighbors = 15,   n_threads = 1,   ret_nn = TRUE,   ret_extra = "fgraph" ) library(vizier)  xy <- fit$embedding species <- iris$Species palette <- c(setosa = "#0072B2", versicolor = "#D55E00", virginica = "#009E73") edges <- embed_edges(fit$fgraph) #> Loading required namespace: Matrix between <- subset(edges, species[from] != species[to])

title: Graph overlays on an iris UMAP
text: quick way thin plot keep one neighbor per flower. fit$nn[[1]] lists neighbors four original measurements order distance. first panel uses nearest neighbor list second uses furthest. embed_edges() skips flower row ID, different flower zero distance still counts. Two flowers can choose , count_bridges() counts pair .  Keeping nearest neighbor gives 5 distinct cross-species pairs. Keeping furthest gives 11. Either way, miss plenty connections fitted graph. pick tenth neighbor specifically, use embed_edges(nn, select = "furthest", k = 10).
code: nn <- fit$nn[[1]] nearest <- embed_edges(nn, select = "nearest") furthest <- embed_edges(nn, select = "furthest") views <- list(Nearest = nearest, Furthest = furthest, Fitted = edges)  count_bridges <- function(e) {   cross <- e[species[e$from] != species[e$to], , drop = FALSE]   nrow(unique(data.frame(     a = pmin(cross$from, cross$to),     b = pmax(cross$from, cross$to)   ))) } counts <- vapply(views, count_bridges, integer(1)) par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1)) for (name in names(views)) {   embed_plot(     xy,     species,     overlays = views[[name]],     color_scheme = palette,     fixed_aspect = TRUE,     show_axes = FALSE,     title = sprintf("%s\n%d cross-species pairs", name, counts[[name]])   ) }

title: Graph overlays on an iris UMAP
text: edges drawn, straight lines pile around flowers. right panel ’ll bundle edges give stronger ones ink. Membership weight maps linearly opacity, 0.01 weight 0 0.25 weight 1. prepare_overlay() uses igraph edgebundle compute Hammer paths .  panels connect 1,347 pairs. right panel, nearby paths bend together weaker edges fade. curve can pass close third flower way two flowers actually connects. embed_ggplot() can use hammer stands, paths continuous edge opacity. colorbar shows fraction neighbors flower kept.  Plotly uses one line trace per distinct opacity. continuous opacity, ’d need 1,208 traces graph. Set alpha_bins = 4L copy hammer path gets nearest four opacities (0.01, 0.09, 0.17 0.25). Now Plotly can draw graph four traces. still gets every sampled point along path, can still hover flower read score.
code: weighted_hammer <- list(   edges = edges,   route = "hammer",   alpha = "weight",   alpha_limits = c(0, 1),   alpha_range = c(0.01, 0.25) ) hammer <- prepare_overlay(xy, weighted_hammer) par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1)) embed_plot(   xy,   retained,   overlays = edges,   limits = c(0, 1),   color_scheme = "grDevices::Viridis",   fixed_aspect = TRUE,   show_axes = FALSE,   title = "Straight edges" ) embed_plot(   xy,   retained,   overlays = hammer,   limits = c(0, 1),   color_scheme = "grDevices::Viridis",   fixed_aspect = TRUE,   show_axes = FALSE,   title = "Weighted Hammer paths" ) embed_ggplot(   xy,   retained,   overlays = hammer,   limits = c(0, 1),   color_scheme = "grDevices::Viridis",   fixed_aspect = TRUE ) +   ggplot2::labs(colour = "Fraction retained") hammer_plotly <- hammer hammer_plotly$alpha_bins <- 4L embed_plotly(   xy,   retained,   overlays = hammer_plotly,   limits = c(0, 1),   color_scheme = "grDevices::Viridis",   fixed_aspect = TRUE,   tooltip = sprintf(     "%s | %d of 10 neighbors retained",     species,     round(10 * retained)   ) )

code: # Embed with PCA pca_iris <- stats::prcomp(iris[, -5], retx = TRUE, rank. = 2) # Visualize the resulting embedding, colored by iris species, using the # rainbow color scheme embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris$Species,   color_scheme = rainbow,   title = "iris PCA", sub = "rainbow colors" )   # topo.colors scheme embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris$Species, color_scheme = topo.colors)   # Pass in data frame and it will use the last (in this case, only) factor # column it finds embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris)   # Use the "Dark2" RColorBrewer scheme embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris, color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Dark2")   # Can plot the category names instead of points, but looks bad if they're # long (or the dataset is large) embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris$Species, cex = 0.5, text = iris$Species)   # Visualize numeric value (petal length) as a color embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris$Petal.Length, color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Blues")   # Just show the points with the 10 longest petals embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris$Petal.Length, color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Blues", top = 10)   # Can force axes to be equal size to stop clusters being distorted in one # direction embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris$Petal.Length,   color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Blues",   equal_axes = TRUE )   # Use supplied limits and equal physical units; use shapes # as an additional category cue embed_plot(pca_iris$x, iris$Species,   xlim = c(-4, 4), ylim = c(-2, 2), fixed_aspect = TRUE,   pch = c(16, 17, 15)[as.integer(iris$Species)] )

code: if (FALSE) { # interactive() # Embed with PCA pca_iris <- stats::prcomp(iris[, -5], retx = TRUE, rank. = 2)  # Load the plotly package library("plotly")  # Visualize the resulting embedding, colored by iris species, using the # rainbow color scheme embed_plotly(pca_iris$x, iris$Species,   color_scheme = rainbow,   title = "iris PCA" )  # topo.colors scheme embed_plotly(pca_iris$x, iris$Species, color_scheme = topo.colors)  # Pass in data frame and it will use the last (in this case, only) factor # column it finds embed_plotly(pca_iris$x, iris)  # Don't have to see a legend if the tooltips will do embed_plotly(pca_iris$x, iris, show_legend = FALSE)  # Custom tooltips embed_plotly(pca_iris$x, iris, tooltip = paste("Species:", iris$Species))  # Use the "Dark2" RColorBrewer scheme embed_plotly(pca_iris$x, iris, color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Dark2")  # Can plot the category names instead of points, but looks bad if they're # long (or the dataset is large) embed_plotly(pca_iris$x, iris$Species, cex = 0.5, text = iris$Species)  # Visualize numeric value (petal length) as a color embed_plotly(pca_iris$x, iris$Petal.Length, color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Blues")  # Can force axes to be equal size to stop cluster being distorted in one # direction embed_plotly(pca_iris$x, iris$Petal.Length,   color_scheme = "RColorBrewer::Blues",   equal_axes = TRUE ) }

text: Added fixed_aspect three renderers preserve equal physical X/Y units caller-supplied coordinate limits. Use full pc_axes argument name: abbreviation pc now ambiguous pch. Fixed numeric coloring num_colors = NULL num_colors = 1 embed_plot(), embed_ggplot(), embed_plotly(). Automatic color selection data frames now skips -missing color columns finds suitable character columns even later column contains identifiers. Named palettes longer require colors unused factor levels. Generated palettes keep color assignments levels unused. embed_ggplot() now scales existing color transparency alpha_scale, embed_plotly() applies alpha_scale text labels.
